newsitem.title: USA: Morris CEO ordered to answer tobacco queries.
newsitem.headline: Morris CEO ordered to answer tobacco queries.

text.p: Philip Morris Cos Inc's Chief Executive Geoffrey Bible was ordered on Monday to answer the pretrial questions from lawyers suing tobacco companies on behalf of non-smoking flight attendants claiming to have been injured by second-hand cigarette smoke.

But a lawyer for Philip Morris said during the hearing by Dade County Circuit Court Judge Robert Kaye that his order was likely to be challenged in a New York Court and that Bible was not likely to be available for questioning until early May.

Stanley Rosenblatt, one of the lawyers pressing the class action suit on behalf of an estimated 60,000 sick flight attendants, said he needed to question Bible because he is a leading Philip Morris spokesman on tobacco policy matters.

Attorneys for Philip Morris said in a hearing that Bible was the head of the Philip Morris parent organization and had no direct responsibilities in the cigarette manufacturing business which is a defendant in the class action suit.
Next week, Rosenblatt is scheduled to question in New York the heads of cigarette units of Philip Morris and other companies.
The judge also ordered that several of the questions and answers to arise from these pretrial sessions in New York be kept secret.
David Hardy, a lawyer for Philip Morris, said that some of the questioning next week would be based on privileged industry documents and the answers should be kept secret.

Kaye also appointed two Florida lawyers, Michael Salmon and Irvin Block, to review in private the large numbers of tobacco industry documents which may or may not be used during the trial scheduled to begin on June 2.
